exact_scope: Prove or falsify the finite-dimensional MLE/ERM claim for approximately i.i.d. state-action-horizon-outcome tuples under non-informative right censoring, correct specification or a stated KL-minimizer target, identifiability, smoothness, an interior true parameter, uniform laws/envelopes, and nonsingular information; establish consistency and n^(-1/2) asymptotic normality, with inverse Fisher covariance only under correct specification.
decision_basis: The paper states a finite-dimensional parametric MLE result, so exact-scope evidence can be constructed as algebraic and probabilistic proof certificates without benchmark training.

The paper names i.i.d.-style sampling, non-informative censoring, identifiability, and smoothness; a faithful proof must make the additional compactness/interiority, domination, uniform-convergence, and nonsingular-information conditions explicit.
A primary derivation and an independent reconstruction from primitive likelihood derivatives can check consistency, score centering, Hessian convergence, and the covariance qualification.
Non-identifiability and singular-information counterexamples provide destructive controls; a small Monte Carlo experiment alone would remain toy.
